codes.evidence_quote: Antonio Mirena Has Not Died, Flamenco Has Not Died. Flamenco will live in the soul of those
codes.target: Antonio Mairena and flamenco as a continuing living art
codes.rationale: The passage turns Mairena's memory into a claim of flamenco survival and continuity across living souls.

codes.evidence_quote: I FEEL GITANO! I feel gitano in the broadest sense of the word; I feel united with an history which makes me (feel) responsible.
codes.target: gitano identity as a mode of belonging to flamenco history
codes.rationale: The speaker uses gitano identity to frame belonging, historical responsibility, and affective identification with flamenco.

codes.evidence_quote: many thanks to all those, who in one way or another, feel united in spirit, to the philosophy of the flamenco art
codes.target: the community united around flamenco art
codes.rationale: The passage constructs a shared community of people spiritually united around flamenco and its continuation.

possible_but_not_emitted.reason: The text is memorial and continuity-oriented, but it does not clearly frame flamenco as public heritage, safeguarding, or collective heritage management.

derived_analysis.target: Antonio Mairena, flamenco survival, and a flamenco community of belonging

annotation_notes: Coded only the visible memorial/manifesto language, not the title metadata.
